newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares close lower on interim profit woes.
newsitem.headline: China B shares close lower on interim profit woes.

text.p: China B shares ended lower on Monday, dragged down by a weaker domestic A share market and institutional selling of stocks expected to post poor 1997 interim results, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index shed 1.349 points or 1.78 percent to 74.285 on volume of 11.882 million shares worth $4.011 million, compared with $5.670 million on Friday.
The A index slid 30.643 points or 2.50 percent to 1,193.397 on turnover of 3.29 billion yuan against Friday's 3.4 billion yuan.
The Shenzhen index of B shares for foreign investors shed 1.23 points or 0.94 percent to 130.03 on thin turnover of HK$33 million against HK$31 million last Friday.
The A share index of China's southern bourse tumbled 13.66 points or 3.35 percent to 394.46 points, with turnover contracting to 5.0 billion yuan from 5.8 billion on Friday.
Brokers said many investors were concerned about the interim results of listed firms, which must publish their first half results by the end of August.
"The weaker A share market helped dampen B share market sentiment," one broker said. "And more overseas selling today dragged the index down," he added.
"B shares fell because of the bearishness of A shares," said a broker at China Southern Securities Co. "Investors did not actively participate in trading due to a lack of confidence."
Brokers said Shenzhen A shares were depressed in the absence of powerful players such as state banks and listed firms.
In May, Beijing barred these major participants from share trading as part of a series of measures aimed at cooling the nation's overheated bourses.
On the Shenzhen B share market, conglomerate Shenzhen Zhonghao (Group) Co Ltd was the biggest loser, sliding HK$0.26, its daily maximum of 10 percent, to HK$2.32 on thin volume of 15,500 shares.

Bengang Steel Plate topped the active list with a volume of 2.3 million shares as it lost HK$0.07 to HK$2.03. The newcomer has fallen below its offer price of HK$2.38 since its debut earlier this month.

Shanghai Erfangji Co was the most actively traded issue on the Shanghai B share market as institutions dumped the company's shares on concerns over its interim results. It fell $0.006 or 5.66 percent to $0.100 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development was the second most actively traded B share issue on domestic selling.
Brokers said it too suffered from expectations of weak interim results and it slid $0.030 or 2.43 percent to $1.200 on volume of 806,600 shares.
Shanghai's A share index continued to fall as market sentiment was weak with many institutional investors jittery over the possibility of further market-cooling measures by regulators.
The SSE30 blue chip index slumped 125.260 points or 3.37 percent to 3,596.439 points.
